common.style_usage: Stardew Valley building pixel art: palette, outline weight, how the roofs are shaded in rows of tiles or shingles with light ridges, dark gable edges and deep shadow under the eaves, and the high top-down front camera where the roof fills over half the building
common.reference_usage: camera, silhouette and roof planes: the lighter roof colour is roof facing up toward the viewer, the darker is roof facing forward, the darkest band is the shadow under the eaves; keep this outline, these openings, and the roof taking more than half the height

old_rtudio_r1.description: An old, empty artists' studio in Stardew Valley pixel art, a little run-down but sturdy: a grey-green slate roof with a large slanted north-light window boarded over with planks, pale stone walls with moss at the base, a big front window boarded up with crossed planks, a narrow wooden door, a faded painted sign board above the door with no text. STRICTLY FRONT-FACING like every Stardew Valley building: the front wall seen square-on and flat, no side walls visible, not turned or rotated, no three-quarter or isometric angle; the roof seen from above and in front, a steep front-gabled roof whose ridge runs back away from the viewer, two big shingled roof planes (lit on the left, shaded on the right) filling about 60% of the height. Building only, nothing around it, no ground, no text, transparent background. The whole building fits inside the picture with a little space above the roof's ridge: draw the complete roof, nothing cut off.
